messages:
kamesh: Heads up — we need to lock down who can download privileged audit bundles. Security wants a minimal approval + justification flow before any full tenant export is allowed. Thoughts on API shape and console UX?

liz: +1. Two quick design axes: (1) interactive console flow with an approval modal and optional manager sign-off, (2) API-friendly workflow for programmatic requests with a temporary access token.

anna: For the console: show a compact summary of filters (time range, resources, actor filters) and require a short rationale field. Also surface an estimated token/size and a retention TTL for the bundle.

nate: How about putting a quota on these privileged downloads per org and per-actor? E.g., 3 full-exports per 30 days per org, and 1 per-actor, with an audit trail for each download. Makes it harder to exfiltrate.

omar: Agree on quotas. Also we should instrument telemetry events so SRE and secops get alerted on high-volume activity. Suggest events like `audit.export.requested`, `audit.export.approved`, `audit.export.downloaded` with metadata: requestor, approver, filters, size_estimate, retention_ttl.

kamesh: Nice. API sketch:
```
POST /v1/platform/audit/exports
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
Body: {
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "time_range": {"from":"2025-11-01T00:00:00Z","to":"2025-11-07T23:59:59Z"},
  "filters": {"routes":["/policy/*"], "actors": ["u-789"]},
  "justification": "Incident investigation #INC-502",
  "retention_ttl_hours": 72
}
```
Return: 202 accepted with `export_request_id` and `approval_required: true|false`. If approval required, response includes `approval_url` and `estimated_size_bytes`.

liz: For approval backend we can integrate with the existing RBAC/approvals service. Proposal: approval rules = (role in privileged_roles) OR (manager_approval). Also allow auto-approval for dedicated enterprise customers if they have a policy flag.

anna: Console affordance: when a request is pending, show a diffs-like preview of the query (sample first 3 events) redacted. That helps approvers evaluate without granting full data. Small code snippet for preview endpoint:
```
GET /v1/platform/audit/exports/{id}/preview
Response: { "sample_events": ["<redacted>"] }
```

nate: Preview is neat but be careful with leaking PII. The preview must run through the same redaction pipeline as exports. Also add a telemetry tag `preview_used=true` on the request.

omar: About retention: we should expire the downloadable bundle after `retention_ttl_hours`. Also keep an immutable audit record in the control plane (no redaction) but with restricted access for compliance. That way we can prove who downloaded what.

kamesh: UX question: do we surface the `estimated_size_bytes` and cost estimate inline? Security might prefer hiding size to avoid info leaks. Product likes surfacing cost to nudge users. Compromise? show size bucket: small/medium/large and a cost range.

liz: I vote for buckets. Small exact sizes can leak activity patterns. Buckets + approximate token cost is actionable.

anna: +1 buckets. Also show the last 3 approvers for that org and how long approvals typically take. Helps set expectations.

nate: Implementation note: throttling should be enforced at the API gateway layer and also at the export worker queue. Add a check in the request path to decrement the org's remaining-exports quota atomically. If no quota, return 429 with guidance and appeal link.

omar: Telemetry fields proposal (flat list): `export_request_id`, `tenant_id`, `requestor_id`, `approver_id`, `filters_hash`, `estimated_size_bucket`, `retention_ttl_hours`, `preview_used`, `result`(approved/denied/expired). Keep payload small.

kamesh: Who owns building the approval modal + API contract? I'll take API contract + gateway checks. @liz want the modal and console copy?

liz: I can take the modal and copy. I'll pair with anna on the preview/redaction UX.

anna: I'll own preview endpoint and ensure redaction parity. Will add unit tests for PII scrubbing.

nate: I'll wire in quotas and queue-level throttles. Also add a new SLO: export-request-approval-latency P99 < 4h for on-call visibility.

omar: I'll add telemetry events to the ingestion pipeline and dashboard tiles for high-volume export signals. Also add a Correlation ID into logs: `audit_export:{export_request_id}`.

dev-bot: deploy scheduled: feature/audit-export-approvals -> staging at 2025-11-05T03:00:00Z :rocket:

kamesh: Great. Action items: (1) liz/anna design modal + preview mock (due EOD Friday), (2) kamesh API contract PR (draft by Monday), (3) nate quota impl spike + SLO PR, (4) omar telemetry schema and dashboard stub. We'll sync in the weekly infra sync.

liz: one more: how do we handle subpoenas / legal holds? Probably separate path that bypasses quotas but requires legal token + stronger logging. Add note to ADR.

kamesh: Good call — add legal path to ADR and require `legal_token` header validated against legal service. No quota but elevated monitoring.

anna: I'll ensure preview endpoint returns an opaque `preview_token` that expires in 15m and is logged as part of the export_request record.

nate: OK. I'll also add a simple migration to seed `org_export_quota` in the billing DB with defaults: 3/month.

kamesh: Thanks everyone. If you have objections, flag them here; otherwise I'll open the API PR and ADR tonight. :thumbsup:
